Growing degree-days from an ensemble of methods

Source: R/ensemble.R
gdd_ensemble.Rd

Usage

gdd_ensemble(
  tmin,
  tmax,
  weights,
  base = 10,
  upper = NULL,
  cutoff = c("horizontal", "vertical", "intermediate"),
  tmin_next = NULL
)

Arguments

tmin, tmax

Numeric vectors of daily minimum and maximum temperatures (degrees Celsius), of equal length, ordered in time for double methods.

weights

Ensemble weights: an object from gdd_ensemble_weights() or a named numeric vector of non-negative weights (names are degree_days() methods). Weights are rescaled to sum to one.

base

Lower developmental threshold (degrees Celsius).

upper

Optional upper developmental threshold (degrees Celsius).

cutoff

Upper threshold treatment: "horizontal" (default), "vertical" or "intermediate". Ignored when upper is NULL.

tmin_next

Optional numeric vector with the minimum temperature of the following day, used only by double methods.

Value

A data frame with one row per day and columns ensemble (weighted mean), sd (weighted standard deviation between members), min and max (range of the members with non-zero weight) and one column per member method.

Details

Computes the daily degree-days of each member method and their weighted mean, with the spread between members as a measure of method uncertainty. degree_days() with method = "ensemble" returns only the weighted mean.

See also

gdd_ensemble_weights()

Examples

w <- c(average = 0.3, single_triangle = 0.7)  # illustrative weights
gdd_ensemble(c(5, 8, 12), c(22, 25, 30), weights = w, base = 10)
#>    ensemble         sd  min       max average single_triangle
#> 1  4.014706 0.33695410  3.5  4.235294     3.5        4.235294
#> 2  6.582353 0.05391266  6.5  6.617647     6.5        6.617647
#> 3 11.000000 0.00000000 11.0 11.000000    11.0       11.000000
